OVERVIEW

Two on-site polls, one clear story

ZigPoll ran two short on-site surveys on tharaa.shop. Together they capture both sides of the purchase decision: why visitors abandon before checkout, and what information shoppers say they need before they'll buy.

05 / 08
THE KEY INSIGHT

“Too expensive” often means “I'm not yet convinced it's worth it”

SURVEY 1 FINDING

17.3% leave because there isn't enough product info or usage guidance on the page.

→
SURVEY 2 FINDING

The same three topics — usage, results timeline, and purity — make up 63% of what shoppers say they need before buying.

→
WHAT IT MEANS

Price objections are inflated by an information gap. Closing that gap is cheaper and faster than any pricing change.

06 / 08
RECOMMENDATIONS · PART 1

Quick wins (low effort, high impact)

01

Rebuild product pages around 4 questions

Add clear “How to use,” “What it treats,” “When you'll see results,” and “Purity / sourcing” sections to every product — directly answers 87% of Survey 2.

02

Introduce a visible entry-level offer

A first-order discount, bundle, or buy-2-get-1 promo shown before exit — requested repeatedly and targets the #1 exit reason (57.6%).

03
Exists

Add “shop by concern” navigation

Let shoppers filter by skin/hair concern instead of product name — addresses the 20.7% who couldn't find what they wanted.

04

Show live stock status + restock alerts

Rose oil, rosehip oil and tea-tree oil were named repeatedly as sold out — a “notify me” button recaptures that demand.

07 / 08
RECOMMENDATIONS · PART 2

Medium-term moves (build on the momentum)

05

Launch a “find your routine” helper

A short quiz or WhatsApp consultation for shoppers who explicitly asked someone to recommend the right products for them.

06

Offer trial / travel sizes

Smaller sizes at accessible price points soften the “expensive for so little” friction without discounting full-size margin.

07

Publish certifications & sourcing

Lab-test results and an ingredient-sourcing story build the trust that a market full of counterfeit “natural” products has eroded.

08
Exists

Set and advertise a free-shipping threshold

Shipping cost and unclear delivery terms came up repeatedly, especially for orders outside Cairo and international orders.

08 / 08

MOBILE SESSION RECORDINGS
CLARITY · MOBILE

Where mobile shoppers focus, scroll, and click

Microsoft Clarity heatmaps and click maps from the mobile product page. Only 25.7% of visitors scroll far enough to see the Add-to-Cart section — these seven findings explain where attention leaks, and what to fix first.

01

Only 25.7% of visitors reach Add to Cart

Attention thins out steadily with every scroll. By the point a shopper would need to hit Add to Cart, roughly three out of four have already dropped off. So we're implementing a sticky Add to Cart bar that shows once the main Add to Cart button scrolls out of view.

02

Utilizing the thumbnail carousel

We're adding to what the carousel shows: it'll surface content pulled from How to Use, What Will Change, and the Ingredients section, the sections shoppers look for most based on the heatmaps.

03

The consent banner takes too many clicks to clear

It's less relevant for non-EU visitors — which is most of Tharaa's audience — so we're rolling out a rule to only show the banner to users browsing from Europe.

04

Delay the WhatsApp icon until the explanatory sections

The icon shouldn't show before a shopper has a reason to ask a question. Scrolling down to the explanatory sections is itself a signal they might need support — showing the icon from that point on makes it more contextually relevant.

05

Move “How to Use” above “What Will Change”

“How to Use” is shorter, easier to scan, and it shows in the numbers — this section already holds attention well. Leading with it should carry that momentum into the sections below.

06

Add more UGC to this section

People engage a lot in this section. Since it already has educational videos, it needs more UGC here as well.

CHECKOUT FUNNEL
GA4 · FUNNEL EXPLORATION

The product page is where every funnel loses shoppers

Four funnel configurations tested in GA4 — with or without the PLP (category page) and Cart step. In every version, the product page (PDP) has by far the highest abandonment rate.
